root_cause.text: alloc_frozen_pages_nolock() in the mm/page_alloc allocator incorrectly assumed spin_trylock() would prevent lock reentry, but on UP (!CONFIG_SMP) in NMI context spin_trylock() always succeeds, allowing reentrant rmqueue() acquisition of the same zone lock and freelist corruption.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that on UP kernels “spin_trylock() is a no-op that unconditionally succeeds even when the lock is already held,” causing alloc_frozen_pages_nolock() from NMI to “re-enter rmqueue() and acquire the zone lock that the interrupted context is already holding, corrupting the freelists,” and the patch adds `if (!IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_SMP) && in_nmi()) return NULL;`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent nolock frozen-page allocation from NMI context on UP systems to avoid incorrect spin_trylock-based reentrancy.
intent_record.what: A new conditional early-return was added in alloc_frozen_pages_nolock_noprof(): after the existing PREEMPT_RT hardirq/NMI check, the code now returns NULL when CONFIG_SMP is disabled and the current context is NMI, with an explanatory comment about spin_trylock() always succeeding on UP even when already locked.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the function from attempting the nolock frozen-page allocation path from NMI context on uniprocessor builds, avoiding unsafe lock acquisition behavior caused by spin_trylock() trivially succeeding on UP and thereby preventing incorrect reentrant access in that context.

grouping_result.intent: Prevent nolock frozen-page allocation from NMI context on UP systems to avoid incorrect spin_trylock-based reentrancy.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets the root cause: on UP in NMI context, spin_trylock() can incorrectly permit reentrant zone-lock acquisition during alloc_frozen_pages_nolock(). Preventing nolock frozen-page allocation in that context is a direct mitigation of the described freelist corruption issue.

candidates.rationale: This conditional only blocked NMI/hardirq use of the nolock allocation path on PREEMPT_RT. The vulnerability exists because on UP systems in NMI context the function still proceeded, relying on spin_trylock() to prevent reentry when it would always succeed, enabling reentrant zone-lock acquisition and freelist corruption.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition restricted rejection of the nolock frozen-page allocation path to PREEMPT_RT builds only. As a result, on UP non-SMP systems in NMI context the function could still proceed into the nolock path, incorrectly relying on spin_trylock() to block reentrant zone-lock acquisition even though spin_trylock() always succeeds there, leading to freelist corruption.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the newly introduced trylock-based allocation path and the exact locking behavior in the allocator fast paths. The root cause is reentrant zone-lock acquisition via spin_trylock on UP/NMI. This commit introduces that behavior for opportunistic allocations by setting `unsigned int alloc_flags = ALLOC_TRYLOCK;` in `try_alloc_pages_noprof()`, then calling `get_page_from_freelist(alloc_gfp, order, alloc_flags, &ac);`. In the zone-locking paths, both `rmqueue_bulk()` and `rmqueue_buddy()` now do `if (!spin_trylock_irqsave(&zone->lock, flags)) { if (unlikely(alloc_flags & ALLOC_TRYLOCK)) return ...; spin_lock_irqsave(&zone->lock, flags); }`, which means that when `ALLOC_TRYLOCK` is set they rely on `spin_trylock_irqsave(&zone->lock, flags)` succeeding as the gate for safe entry. There is no check here for the UP/!CONFIG_SMP reentrancy case described in the root cause. The only bailout added is `if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT) && (in_nmi() || in_hardirq())) return NULL;`, which addresses PREEMPT_RT hardirq/NMI safety, not the stated bug on UP where `spin_trylock()` always succeeds in NMI and allows reentry of the same `zone->lock`. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix for the reported root cause is not present in this commit.
